theme: Population, migration and second-home data (IRS migration, Census CPS, USPS change of address, second-home counts, holiday-home shares Europe)
queries_run: gh search repos "IRS migration data" --sort stars
gh search repos "USPS change of address" --sort stars
gh search repos "county to county migration" --sort stars
gh search repos "moving migration data USA" --sort stars
gh search repos "vacation rental second home Europe" --sort updated
gh search repos "domestic migration flows" --sort stars

candidates.name: Hurricanes_and_Migration
candidates.what_it_holds: Complete time series of US county-to-county migration flows 1998-2015 built from IRS-SOI data: aggregate outflow.csv/inflow.csv files plus per-year matrices (files coded e.g. '9899in'/'9899out') for every year pair 1998-2015, county FIPS granularity. Also a JSON of FEMA-declared hurricanes 1990-2018 by county FIPS with costs/deaths/dates, used to study migration response to disasters.
candidates.why_useful: Long, clean, ready-to-use IRS migration panel (1998-2015) at county level -- can be extended/joined with post-2015 IRS SOI vintages to build a second-home / relocation proxy for STR demand in destination counties (sunbelt/vacation-market in-migration), and the hurricane-shock design is a template for isolating migration-driven demand shifts.
candidates.size_hint: ~18 annual matrix pairs + 2 aggregate CSVs + 1 JSON

candidates.name: IRS-migration-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Raw IRS SOI migration files ('seven legacy formats', 2,000+ files) under MigData/, standardized into one flat file DATA-PROCESSED/county_migration_data.txt with ORIGIN (county FIPS), DESTINATION (state FIPS) and annual migrant counts, 1990-2010. Small-flow cells (<10 filers) coded 99999.
candidates.why_useful: Pre-cleaned 1990-2010 IRS migration panel, MIT-licensed, useful to backfill migration history before the 1998-2015 series above and cross-check destination-county in-migration trends against Airbnb-heavy vacation/second-home markets.

candidates.name: county-migration
candidates.what_it_holds: IRS SOI county-to-county migration lookup tool for the 2010-2011 tax year (most recent year IRS published this format at county level): inflow/outflow counts, net migration, top origin/destination counties, and average AGI per flow, US counties.
candidates.why_useful: Adds average-AGI-by-migration-flow, a rough proxy for the income level of movers into second-home/vacation destination counties -- useful for wealth-segment demand context, though only a single-year snapshot.

candidates.name: migration-flow-tool
candidates.what_it_holds: County-to-county migration pattern tool built on IRS tax data (SOI migration files); appears to be a processing/visualization tool rather than a large bundled historical archive -- not independently verified beyond repo description.
candidates.why_useful: Recently updated (Aug 2026) IRS-migration tooling could point to a newer IRS SOI vintage/pull method than the 2015-era archives above.
candidates.time_coverage: unknown (recent IRS SOI vintage, per description)

candidates.name: IRS_Migration
candidates.what_it_holds: Exploration of state-to-state and county-to-county IRS migration data (not independently verified for committed files beyond description).
candidates.why_useful: Another independent IRS-SOI ingestion example; low priority given older last-activity date and unverified data presence.

candidates.name: flood_claim_migrations
candidates.what_it_holds: Maps/models National Flood Insurance Program claims against county-to-county IRS migration flows by year; likely bundles or references NFIP claims data plus IRS migration data (not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: Climate-driven relocation into/out of coastal vacation-home markets (a known second-home demand driver) -- template and possibly data for linking flood risk to migration.

candidates.name: migration_flow_map
candidates.what_it_holds: Visualization tool for county-to-county US migration flows; likely consumes Census/IRS migration data rather than bundling a novel dataset (not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: Possible pointer to a Census-based migration-flow source/pipeline as an alternative to IRS SOI.

candidates.name: population-demographics-de-project
candidates.what_it_holds: Data-engineering pipeline combining Census ACS, TIGER/Line, and IRS migration data (2012-2024) at state/county/tract granularity into an interactive mapping tool; described as a pipeline rather than a static committed dataset (not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: If it bundles a processed 2012-2024 IRS-migration table, it would be the most recent multi-year panel found in this sweep, extending well past the other repos' 2015 cutoff -- worth a follow-up directory listing.

candidates.name: InvestmentProperty
candidates.what_it_holds: Real-estate investment analysis dashboard combining IRS migration data with backtested appreciation models and interactive visualizations; likely a consumer of migration data rather than a novel archive (not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: Could reveal a migration-to-home-price-appreciation model relevant to second-home market strength in destination markets, but content unverified.

candidates.name: IRS-Migration-Outflow
candidates.what_it_holds: Code to convert abstractly-presented IRS migration data into a unified county-to-county outflow dataset; a processing script for raw IRS SOI files rather than a distinct archive (not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: Alternative/newer ingestion method for IRS SOI outflow data, potentially covering more recent years than the 2015-era archives.

candidates.name: DMIG (Domestic Migration Information Germany)
candidates.what_it_holds: Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI) for analyzing and visualizing annual domestic migration flows within Germany; likely built on official German statistical office (Destatis) migration series rather than bundling a large novel dataset (not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: A European domestic-migration analogue; Germany is a large Airbnb / holiday-home market, and internal migration toward coastal/alpine regions is a plausible second-home demand signal, but this repo's own data content is unconfirmed.

candidates.name: model_detailed_migration_flows
candidates.what_it_holds: GLA model to estimate missing detailed origin-destination domestic migration flows for London population projections; a modeling methodology repo, likely referencing ONS internal migration statistics rather than bundling a full novel dataset (not independently verified).
candidates.why_useful: Official-statistics-adjacent UK internal migration modeling; London/UK second-home and short-let markets are relevant to ABNB's Europe segment, but low direct data yield expected.

candidates.name: Analysis-of-domestic-migration-flows-in-Finland
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis notebook/repo on Finnish domestic migration flows, presumably drawing on Statistics Finland data; content not independently verified for committed raw data files.
candidates.why_useful: Finland has a very high holiday-home ownership rate (relevant European comparator for holiday-home share stats) but this repo is a small personal analysis with no confirmed bundled dataset -- marginal.

notes: USPS change-of-address search returned zero results in two attempts ('USPS change of address' and implicitly via other terms) -- USPS COTA data is not publicly released in bulk and apparently has no GitHub mirror; treat this as a confirmed dead end for this theme, not an oversight. No repos surfaced for 'second homes dataset' / 'vacation rental second home Europe' / Eurostat holiday-home-share specifically -- European second-home/holiday-home share data (Eurostat, INSEE 'residences secondaires', ONS second-address statistics) appears to have no dedicated GitHub mirrors found via these queries; a follow-up scout could try French/Spanish-language terms ('residences secondaires', 'segunda vivienda') or Eurostat-specific repo topics. Census CPS/ACS migration-specific repos did not surface distinctly from the IRS-migration-dominated results; a targeted re-run with 'Census ACS migration' or '--topic=migration' might do better but was outside the 6-call budget. Best finds by far are eugeniopaglino/Hurricanes_and_Migration (clean 1998-2015 IRS county panel, MIT-adjacent) and mathewhauer/IRS-migration-data (1990-2010, MIT). Both would need extension with post-2015 IRS SOI vintages (available directly from irs.gov, not GitHub) to be current enough for the 2026 pitch.
